title: 3 Claude Code commands most people never use: /compact to sh

plan.visualBrief: A tilted glass code editor: three files snap red and broken, /rewind is typed below, and a green U-turn arrow sweeps up as the files flip back to clean.

scenes.vo: Claude Code just broke three files? One command undoes it.

plan.visualBrief: A dock with three empty numbered slots drops in while a big tilted Claude Code card counts up to 3 commands, a blurred terminal behind it.

scenes.vo: It's one of three Claude Code commands most people never use.

plan.visualBrief: Slot 1 fills with /rewind; in a tilted terminal the command runs, three red files roll back their edits one by one and flip green.

scenes.vo: First, slash rewind. Type it, and Claude Code undoes its last changes. Those three broken files? Clean again.

plan.visualBrief: Slot 2 fills with /compact; a tall, heavy chat history at 184k tokens squeezes into a short summary block at 12k while a glowing thread line from start to now stays unbroken.

scenes.vo: Second, slash compact. When a session gets long and heavy, it shrinks it down, without losing the thread of what you're building.

plan.visualBrief: Slot 3 fills with Plan mode; big Shift and Tab keys press down, then a numbered plan card unfolds while three file tiles beside it lock with padlocks.

scenes.vo: Third, plan mode. Press Shift Tab, and Claude shows you its plan first. Not a single file is touched until you're happy with it.

plan.visualBrief: The finished three-command dock shrinks up, a glass comment bubble pops in, then a big orange Follow button lands below it and pulses.

scenes.vo: Drop a comment if you want more Claude Code tips like these, and follow so you don't miss the next one.

storyPlan.premise: 3 Claude Code commands most people never use: /compact to shrink a long session without losing the thread, /rewind to undo the last changes, and plan mode (Shift+Tab) to see the plan before any file is touched. Show each one working.
